verdict.rationale: cubic runs several of its own behaviors autonomously in the background once enabled: automatic PR reviews on install, auto-approval of low-risk PRs (shadow mode, then live), automatic thread resolution, automatic issue-requirement analysis, and a wiki kept current through a rolling PR. These are fixed, event-triggered review features rather than user-defined automations; custom agents are review rules, not arbitrary background jobs. missing for 10: user-defined automation workflows with custom triggers or actions, recurring/scheduled runs (e.g. scheduled codebase scans), and independent or hands-on corroboration of autonomous operation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Once installed, cubic automatically reviews new pull requests.
cubic can approve clean pull requests automatically when your repository policy allows it. Start in shadow mode to see which PRs cubic would approve, then switch to live mode
Enable automatic thread resolution to close findings when the issue is fixed
cubic can automatically analyze your pull requests to see if they meet the requirements from your linked Linear or Jira issues.
keeps them current through a rolling pull request
